title: Claim Denial Letters — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
**Written denials under NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)**

Tidemark denies a coverage on a claim in writing, stating one denial reason:

| Denial reason | When it is stated |
|---|---|
| Not a Flood Event | The damage did not result from flood as defined |
| Loss During Waiting Period | The loss began before the coverage or increase took effect |
| No Coverage on Date of Loss | The policy was lapsed, cancelled or nullified on the date of loss |
| Proof of Loss Not Timely | Under the proof-of-loss rule |
| Excluded Property | The damaged items are not insured property (including basement contents beyond the listed basement items when the tier does not cover basement contents) |
| Loss Below Deductible | The payable amount is zero after the deductible |

A partial denial covers only the denied coverage and does not stop payment of the others. The denial letter informs the insured that an appeal may be filed with FEMA within the tier's appeal window, in calendar days, of the denial date and that suit must be filed within the tier's suit limitation period, in calendar months, of the denial date; Tidemark does not decide FEMA appeals.

*Hypothetical case.* A claim measures both a building and a contents loss; the contents loss falls below the contents deductible. The contents coverage is denied as Loss Below Deductible, and the building coverage continues to be paid.
